title: Best Term Life Insurance 2026: 5 compared
description: Haven Life, Ladder, Ethos, Fabric by Gerber, Policygenius — same 35-year-old, $500k 20-year term, real quotes. Where the medical exam gets waived, and which insurer underwrote in 48 hours.
lede: Five term life providers. Same 35-year-old non-smoker. $500k 20-year term. This guide compares 5 options using published specifications, manufacturer documentation and independent reviews
methodology: This comparison is desk research. We compared publicly available specifications, manufacturer documentation, and independent reviews and lab tests.

sections.heading: Monthly premium for the same coverage
paragraphs: Monthly premium for $500k 20-year term, 35yo healthy non-smoker: Ethos $28, Haven Life $30, Ladder $31, Fabric $32, Policygenius (best of 5 quotes shopped) $26. Differences shrink for higher-risk applicants — the algorithmic insurers (Ethos, Haven, Ladder, Fabric) flatten quotes around healthy applicants.
$1M 20-year coverage premium: roughly 1.8× the $500k premium. Doubling coverage costs less than 2× — fixed underwriting overhead doesn't scale linearly.

sections.heading: Medical exam waiver
paragraphs: Healthy 35yo no-exam approval: Ethos (instant decision via algorithmic underwriting), Haven Life (instant for amounts up to $1M), Ladder (instant up to $3M), Fabric (instant up to $1M).

Policygenius is a marketplace — they shop your application across 20+ traditional insurers. Most traditional insurers require a medical exam; Policygenius can find no-exam carriers but may not be the cheapest.

Real wait time application-to-coverage: Ethos 48 hours, Haven Life 72 hours, Ladder 24 hours, Fabric 72 hours, Policygenius (traditional carrier) 14-28 days. The algorithmic providers win on speed by 10-25x.

sections.heading: What you give up at each
paragraphs: Ethos, Haven Life, Ladder, Fabric: algorithmic underwriting only. If you have any health complexity, you may be declined automatically.
Policygenius: shops traditional carriers. Better fit for applicants with health conditions (diabetes, BP, etc.) — traditional underwriters can look at medical history nuance.

Long-term consideration: traditional carriers (Northwestern Mutual, MassMutual, etc. via Policygenius) have stronger financial ratings. Algorithmic insurers like Ethos and Ladder are reinsured by AIG, Munich Re — strong but newer track record.

faqs.a: Term for almost everyone. Cheaper, simpler, designed for income-replacement during working years. Whole life only if you have specific estate planning needs and have maxed out other tax-advantaged accounts.

faqs.q: How much coverage do I need?
faqs.a: Common rule: 10-12× annual income. For 35yo earning $100k, that's $1M-1.2M. Adjust for mortgage balance and number of dependents.

faqs.q: Can I drop term life later?
faqs.a: Yes — term life has no surrender penalties. Just stop paying premiums and the policy lapses.
Premium stays level for 20 years, then ends. If you outlive the term, no payout. Most people buy term to cover working years (until kids are grown or mortgage paid off).

haven-life-term.review: Haven Life is the right pick for healthy applicants who want instant approval. Owned by MassMutual (strong financial backing), algorithmic underwriting up to $1M, decision in minutes. Premium isn't always cheapest but the speed is best-in-class. App-driven experience.
cons: May decline applicants with any health complexity

ladder-life.review: Ladder Life lets you increase or decrease coverage as life changes (no new underwriting needed). Instant approval up to $3M for healthy applicants. Algorithmic underwriting. Reinsured by AIG. The 'ladder up/down' feature is unique in the category.

ethos-life-insurance.review: Ethos is the cheapest of the algorithmic insurers in our 35yo test ($28/mo for $500k 20-year). Instant decisions, no medical exam for healthy applicants. Reinsured by Munich Re. Good app, simple application.
cons: Decline rate higher than Haven Life

fabric-by-gerber-life.review: Fabric by Gerber Life is positioned for new parents. Includes will-writing feature, child rider available. Premium competitive ($32/mo for our 35yo). Underwritten by Gerber Life — financially solid, but the brand is more associated with infants than adults.
cons: Brand recognition tilted toward baby insurance

policygenius-term-marketplace.review: Policygenius is not an insurer — they're a marketplace that shops your application across 20+ traditional carriers (Northwestern Mutual, Lincoln, Prudential, etc.). Best for applicants with health conditions where traditional underwriting is needed. Takes 2-4 weeks but can find the cheapest absolute quote.

offerNotes.haven-life-term: Apply at havenlife.com. Owned by MassMutual since 2014.
offerNotes.ladder-life: Apply at ladderlife.com. The ladder up/down feature is a real differentiator.
offerNotes.ethos-life-insurance: Apply at ethos.com. Algorithmic-only — apply elsewhere if you have any health complexity.

recommendedFor.label: Young parents who just had their first child
recommendedFor.reason: Fabric includes a built-in will-writing tool and a child rider add-on, making it purpose-built for new parents securing their family's future.

recommendedFor.label: Healthy adults who need coverage fast this week
recommendedFor.reason: Ladder approves up to $3M instantly with no medical exam, covering you in as little as 24 hours — the fastest application-to-coverage.

recommendedFor.label: Budget-conscious earners buying their first policy
recommendedFor.reason: At $28/mo for $500k 20-year coverage, Ethos was the cheapest algorithmic option, with instant decisions and no medical exam for healthy applicants.

recommendedFor.label: Applicants with diabetes, blood pressure, or prior conditions
recommendedFor.reason: Policygenius shops 20+ traditional carriers who apply nuanced medical underwriting, giving complex-health applicants the best shot at approval and competitive rates.

recommendedFor.label: Professionals wanting a financially rock-solid insurer
recommendedFor.reason: Haven Life is backed by MassMutual, one of the highest-rated insurers in the US, combining algorithmic speed with the financial strength of a 170-year-old company.
